E1:
(1) A ProximityPrompt only shows when parented to a BasePart, an Attachment, or a Model with a PrimaryPart (it needs a world position). A Folder inside a model with no PrimaryPart gives it no position, so it never appears. Fix: parent the prompt to a part (e.g. the machine's front panel) or to an Attachment in that part, or set VendingMachine.PrimaryPart and parent the prompt to the Model.
(2) RequiresLineOfSight defaults to true: the prompt raycasts from the camera to the prompt's position and any blocking part (the glass case) hides it. Fix: set RequiresLineOfSight = false, or move the prompt to a part/Attachment outside the glass, or make the glass non-blocking for the check (CanQuery = false, only possible with CanCollide = false). Also check MaxActivationDistance, Enabled, ProximityPromptService.Enabled and that the prompt is not under a descendant of a client-only stream-out region.
E2:
- AlwaysOnTop = false: the gui is depth-tested and hidden behind walls (true draws over all geometry).
- MaxDistance = 100: beyond 100 studs from the camera the billboard is not rendered (default 0/inf = always).
- Size in Scale instead of Offset, e.g. Size = UDim2.fromScale(4, 1) (studs): Scale on a BillboardGui is in studs, so it shrinks with distance like a world object; Offset is pixels and stays constant on screen. Use TextScaled = true on the label so text fits the scaling frame.
- Optional: StudsOffset / StudsOffsetWorldSpace to place it above the head; LightInfluence 0 to keep it readable; DistanceLowerLimit/DistanceUpperLimit/DistanceStep only if you want stepped Offset scaling.
E3:
With CharacterAutoLoads = false the engine never spawns characters: not on join and not on death. RespawnTime only applies to automatic respawns, so it does nothing now. You must call Player:LoadCharacterAsync() (old name LoadCharacter, renamed Jan 2026) yourself on the server:
```lua
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
Players.CharacterAutoLoads = false
local RESPAWN = 3
local function spawn(p) if p.Parent then pcall(function() p:LoadCharacterAsync() end) end end
Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(function(p)
  p.CharacterAdded:Connect(function(char)
    char:WaitForChild("Humanoid").Died:Connect(function()
      task.wait(RESPAWN); spawn(p) -- or wait until round logic allows
    end)
  end)
  spawn(p) -- or spawn when the round starts
end)
```
Connect CharacterAdded before the first load; call it from a server Script only.
E4: Raycasts ignore parts whose CanQuery is false (CanQuery only takes effect when CanCollide is false, which is the case here). Filters cannot bring them back. Fix: set CanQuery = true on the glass (keep CanCollide = false so players walk through). If other queries should ignore the glass, exclude it there via their params (FilterDescendantsInstances/ExcludeInstances) or a collision group; for the laser you can use a dedicated CollisionGroup on RaycastParams, or RespectCanCollide=false (default) so the non-colliding but queryable glass is hit.
E5:
Clone() returns nil when the instance's Archivable is false (Clone skips non-archivable instances and descendants), so template:Clone() is nil and :PivotTo errors. Fix: set Goblin.Archivable = true (or temporarily set it true before cloning and restore it).
Destroy() sets Parent to nil and locks the Parent property permanently (plus disconnects connections), so a destroyed instance can never be reparented: hence "Parent property ... is locked". Never Destroy a template you plan to reuse.
Correct pattern: keep the template in ServerStorage/ReplicatedStorage, Archivable = true, Clone() a fresh copy per spawn, PivotTo, parent to workspace, and Destroy() the clone (not the template) on death. If you need reuse for performance, pool clones and park them by setting Parent = nil or moving them away, not Destroy.

```lua
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local SIZE = Vector3.new(6, 5, 6)
local function swing(attacker: Model)
  local root = attacker:FindFirstChild("HumanoidRootPart"); if not root then return end
  local cf = root.CFrame * CFrame.new(0, 0, -3)
  local params = OverlapParams.new()
  params.FilterType = Enum.RaycastFilterType.Exclude
  params.FilterDescendantsInstances = {attacker}
  local hit = {}
  for _, part in workspace:GetPartBoundsInBox(cf, SIZE, params) do
    local model = part:FindFirstAncestorOfClass("Model")
    local hum = model and model:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid")
    if hum and not hit[model] and hum.Health > 0 then
      hit[model] = true
      hum:TakeDamage(20)
    end
  end
end
```
Caveat: GetPartBoundsInBox tests against each part's axis-aligned bounding box, not exact geometry, so rotated/irregular parts can register slightly outside the box; use GetPartsInPart with a box part for exact (costlier) checks. Server validates cooldown and range; the client only requests the swing.

E15:
Missing parts: by default models stream in part by part. Set the building's ModelStreamingMode = Atomic, then the whole model arrives together and streams out together; in the LocalScript WaitForChild the model itself (not individual descendants). Alternatively Player:RequestStreamAroundAsync(position) before inspecting, or write code that handles parts via ChildAdded/StreamingEnabled-safe patterns.
Scoreboard always present: ModelStreamingMode = Persistent (sent after join, never streamed out; Workspace.PersistentLoaded fires when persistent models are in), or PersistentPerPlayer with Model:AddPersistentPlayer(player) for specific players. Or put pure UI data in ReplicatedStorage/attributes instead of a workspace model.
Trade-offs: Atomic delays the whole model until all parts can be sent and keeps it only while needed; Persistent costs memory/bandwidth on every client and join time, so use sparingly. Player:AddReplicationFocus adds a streaming focus (each costs like an extra player). StreamingMinRadius/TargetRadius tune how much is around the player; StreamOutBehavior/ModelStreamingBehavior Improved affects unused models.
E16:
Aim direction 30x/s: yes, switch to UnreliableRemoteEvent. It is frequent, only the latest value matters, and a lost/out-of-order packet is replaced by the next one, so it saves bandwidth/latency from resends.
Hit reports: keep RemoteEvent (reliable, ordered). A dropped hit is a gameplay/state change; also the server must validate hits (rate, distance, line of sight, ammo) rather than trust them.
Limits on UnreliableRemoteEvent: payload over ~1,000 bytes (after encoding/compression) is dropped; no ordering or delivery guarantee; events sent when no handler is connected are discarded, not queued; when throttled, excess is dropped rather than delayed. Keep payloads to a few numbers (e.g. packed Vector3 or buffer), rate-limit per player on the server and sanity-check values.
E17:
```lua
-- layout: u16 id (2) + 3 x f32 (12) = 14 bytes
local function pack(id: number, pos: Vector3): buffer
  local b = buffer.create(14)
  buffer.writeu16(b, 0, id)
  buffer.writef32(b, 2, pos.X)
  buffer.writef32(b, 6, pos.Y)
  buffer.writef32(b, 10, pos.Z)
  return b
end
local function unpack(b: buffer): (number, Vector3)
  return buffer.readu16(b, 0), Vector3.new(buffer.readf32(b, 2), buffer.readf32(b, 6), buffer.readf32(b, 10))
end
-- server: remote:FireAllClients(pack(id, part.Position))
-- client: remote.OnClientEvent:Connect(function(b) local id, pos = unpack(b) end)
```
Rules: buffers are fixed-size (buffer.create(n), cannot grow; buffer.len); offsets are 0-based byte offsets; reading/writing out of bounds errors; little-endian; writeu16 wraps/truncates values outside 0-65535; f32 loses precision vs Luau's f64 numbers; buffers are mutable and passed by reference, but remotes send a copy; they replicate efficiently through remotes and can be stored in DataStores. Validate buffer length on receipt (buffer.len(b) == 14).
E18:
Unanchored assemblies are simulated by one machine, their network owner. By default the server auto-assigns ownership; when the driver sits in the VehicleSeat the engine usually hands the cart to that player, but automatic ownership can flip between server and driver (e.g. near other players), causing stutter and input lag. The owner's physics replicates to everyone, so the client-owned cart's positions arrive at the server late and interpolated, which is why server Touched on the kill brick fires oddly (late/ghost contacts, and a client owner can also fake positions).
Server fix: when a player sits (Seat.Occupant changes) call cartPrimaryPart:SetNetworkOwner(player) (on any part of the assembly; it applies to the whole assembly; all parts must be unanchored); on exit call SetNetworkOwner(nil) to return it to the server, or SetNetworkOwnershipAuto(). Check CanSetNetworkOwnership() first. Make the kill brick ignore cart parts (check for a Humanoid via GetPlayerFromCharacter) and validate speed/position server-side since the client owns the physics.

E20:
New properties on both RaycastParams and OverlapParams: IncludeInstances and ExcludeInstances (arrays of instances; descendants count). Unlike FilterDescendantsInstances + FilterType (one list, either include or exclude), both can be used at once. IncludeInstances = nil means everything is eligible, {} means nothing; when an instance is in both, exclusion wins. FilterDescendantsInstances/FilterType still work but are superseded; don't mix the old and new styles in one params.
```lua
local params = RaycastParams.new()
params.IncludeInstances = {workspace.Map}
params.ExcludeInstances = {workspace.Map.Glass}
local result = workspace:Raycast(origin, dir, params)
```
Build params once and reuse. Note parts still need CanQuery (when CanCollide = false) to be hit.

E24:
Luau added math.lerp and math.isnan/math.isinf/math.isfinite (2025), alongside the existing math.map and math.clamp/math.sign/math.round.
- math.lerp(a: number, b: number, t: number): number -- a + (b - a) * t, exact at t = 1.
- math.map(x: number, inmin: number, inmax: number, outmin: number, outmax: number): number -- remaps x from [inmin, inmax] to [outmin, outmax] (not clamped; wrap in math.clamp if needed).
These are native/fast and replace hand-written lerp/remap helpers. (Vector/CFrame have their own :Lerp methods.)
